newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh court postpones start of Mujib trial.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh court postpones start of Mujib trial.

text.p: A Dhaka Court on Monday postponed the start of the trial of the alleged killers of Bangladesh's founding father, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, after defence lawyers demanded a higher court hear the case, court officials said.
Judge Qazi Golam Rasul adjourned the hearing until April 29, the officials said. They did not give details.
Twenty people have been charged for alleged involvement in the killing of Mujib in a 1975 army coup, police said on Tuesday.
Mujib was the father of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina and the country's first president upon independence in 1971.
Court officials said the "district and session judge's court" dealing with the case completed drawing up the charges earlier this month and set April 21 for the hearing to begin formally.
The accused, mostly retired army officers, have been charged with murder, conspiracy and concealing evidence, police said.
Only six of the 20 accused had been in custody, police said. The others were believed to have fled the country.
Five of the six, including four ex-army officers and Taheruddin Thakur, who served as Mujib's information minister, appeared in court on Monday.
The trial had to wait until Hasina took office last June because Mujib's successors had introduced a law protecting the masterminds of the 1975 coup from prosecution.
Bangladesh's parliament repealed the "black law" in November last year.
